title: Micro-handoff oncall cheat sheet (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, user-facing scratchpad for testing a 'micro-handoff' oncall pattern: short, repeatable, async-friendly handoffs to reduce cognitive load and make follow-ups faster. Use as a source for a short internal announcement + 2-minute all-hands mention and Slack templates.

Context / why we are trying this:
- Current handoffs often run long (30-60m) and are hard to schedule across timezones.
- We get inbox pileups and lost context after long meetings; follow-ups slip.
- Goal: preserve signal (what to watch, recent incidents, outstanding tasks) while making handoff time minimal and asynchronous-first.

Proposed micro-handoff model (core):
1) Overlap window: 10 minutes (optional voice/zoom). If both people are online, do a 5–10 minute sync.
2) Required async artifact: 3-line summary + 3 bullet list. Template below.
3) Critical incidents: immediate voice/zoom + pager escalation stays the same. Micro-handoff does NOT replace war-room response.
4) Sticky notes: update the oncall ticket (tags: oncall-handoff, owner-change).
5) Follow-up queue: anything that needs >15m becomes a follow-up ticket assigned to the new oncall with a 48h target.

Micro-handoff template (to paste into Slack / pager or ticket):
- 1-line status (OK / Degraded / Major) + impacts (services / customers)
- 1-line what I just handled (incidents mitigated, rollbacks, mitigations still running)
- 1-line top watchlist for next shift (endpoints, dashboards, jobs)
- 3 short bullets: outstanding actions (owner + ETA), config changes pending, escalation shortcuts (who to call)
Example:
STATUS: Degraded — embeddings API 503s for a subset of requests (eu-west-1).
RECENT: Restarted grpc-proxy on node gproxy-12; rate limit throttling reduced traffic but errors still at 1–2%.
WATCH: Watch requests hitting /v1/embeddings and the downstream memcache error rate (dashboard link).
ACTIONS: 1) Follow up with infra to check node gproxy-12 health (Rowan, 3h) 2) Monitor cache hit-rate (Aisha, 1h) 3) If errors >5% escalate to SRE lead (pager).

Slack announcement template (short):
- TL;DR: switching to micro-handoff trial for the next 4 weeks. Oncall shifts still same. Expect 3-line handoff + optional 10m sync. We will measure time-to-first-response, incident follow-up completion and satisfaction. More: <link to survey>.
- Channel: #sre-oncall, DM the incoming oncall with the handoff artifact.

All-hands 2-minute script (CEO/ops brief):
- Quick line: "We’re piloting a faster oncall handoff to reduce interruption fatigue and improve follow-ups across regions. This is a small process change: same coverage, shorter handoff artifacts, clearer follow-up tickets."
- Call out: "If you’re oncall and want to opt-out during complex migrations, tell your manager."

Anticipated questions + suggested answers
Q: Does this reduce overlap for debugging complex incidents?
A: No — complex incidents still trigger full handoffs and war rooms. Micro-handoff is for routine shift transitions.

Q: Will this make things more asynchronous and reduce learning?
A: Good point. We require a minimal artifact that captures context and a follow-up ticket pattern so knowledge doesn’t evaporate. We’ll measure and iterate.

Q: What if the incoming oncall misses something?
A: Pager/escalation unchanged. If the incoming is offline, the outgoing must escalate to the oncall backup and add notes to the ticket.

Rolling experiment plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (pilot kickoff): announce, share template, add a short survey link for feedback.
- Weeks 1–3: run micro-handoffs, collect metrics: average handoff time, % with required template, time to ticket closure for follow-ups, subjective satisfaction (pulse).
- Week 4: retro + decision (rollout, iterate, or revert).

Metrics to collect (minimal):
- % shifts completed with micro-handoff template (target 90%)
- Median handoff duration (baseline vs trial)
- Follow-up ticket completion within 48h (target +10% over baseline)
- Qualitative feedback via 1-question pulse (was handoff adequate? yes/no)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide who owns the measurement dashboard (Rowan volunteered; need confirm).
- Update oncall runbook with template link and examples (owner: Aisha).
- Create survey form and short explanation doc for managers (owner: Hector).
- Add automation: bot posts reminder to complete template at 5min before shift end (ask platform team if feasible).

Edge cases to note:
- Long-running incidents: treat as handoff + war-room. Micro-handoff should include direct bridge link and pager pings.
- Follow-ups across teams: make sure cross-team follow-ups have clear owners (use @mentions in ticket).

Draft Slack snippet to post in #sre-oncall when the trial launches:
"Heads up: starting today we’ll trial a micro-handoff pattern for oncall transitions for 4 weeks. New requirement: post the 3-line handoff template to the oncall ticket and DM the incoming person. Optional 10-min sync if both available. See [confluence link]. Questions: ping @Hector Ramos"

Notes to self (scratchy):
- Keep language short in announcement — people skip long posts.
- Emphasize this is a *trial* and we will iterate.
- Be explicit about what is NOT changing (coverage, pager escalation).

Backchannel links to include in final doc (placeholders):
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/ONCALL-ROTATION
- Pilot Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-OPS-1457
- Survey: https://forms.office.com/placeholder

Version history (scratch):
- 2026-02-20 created (initial idea)
- 2026-02-24 added template and metrics
- 2026-03-01 feedback from Aisha + Rowan: add mandatory 48h follow-up ticket rule
- 2026-03-12 updated Slack text and pilot timeline

Unresolved decisions for leadership:
- Approve 4-week pilot (yes/no)
- Automations: reminder bot — required for rollout?
- Any objections from platform/infra owners about adding bot reminders.

End of scratchpad.
